title: Installation media reference, version 1
description: The declared identity of the installation media a build constructs from. Version-controlled and reviewed before a build runs. This is the input to media qualification, not its result: it states what the media must be, and qualification decides whether the artifact presented has that fingerprint. Qualification never inspects the media's contents.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this contract. Dispatch is a hard-coded map, never a path built from this value.

mediaId.description: A stable identifier for this media reference, used in provenance and evidence.

reference.description: Where the media is obtained from, stated exactly. No discovery, no 'latest'.

kind.description: How the locator is resolved. Only 'file' exists: media is gigabytes and is staged where the build execution context can already read it. Adding a retrieval kind is a schema change, not a value someone may start using.

locator.description: The exact path, URL, or library item the media is obtained from.

fileName.description: The expected file name of the artifact itself, so a locator resolving to a directory cannot silently select a different file.

sizeBytes.description: Optional. A cheap mismatch check before hashing gigabytes, never a substitute for the digest.

integrity.description: The expected digest and where it came from. The digest length is checked against the algorithm during qualification, which no per-field constraint can express.

digest.description: Lowercase hexadecimal. Length is checked against the algorithm during qualification.

authority.description: Where the expected digest was obtained. Independence from the artifact is NOT proven by this contract: it is constrained structurally -- the citation must be an HTTPS reference, which a path beside the media cannot be -- and otherwise attested by the reviewer who approved the reference. Do not read a valid citation as a verified one.

kind.description: Only vendor-published exists. A checksum the media publisher states through a channel separate from the artifact is the single authority this contract accepts; an operator recording a value they read elsewhere is that same vendor-published checksum, and is cited as such rather than given a weaker kind of its own.

citation.description: The HTTPS reference the digest was read from. Structurally validated so it cannot be a path beside the artifact, and specific enough for someone else to look it up.

image.description: The declared installation selection: which image inside the media is intended to be installed. Recorded intent. Nothing in qualification opens the media, so this is not confirmed against its contents at any point in stage 1; the pre-seal checks compare the installed operating system against it.

edition.description: The edition name as the media itself reports it.

index.description: The image index within the media. Stated alongside the edition so qualification can confirm the two agree rather than trusting either alone.

platform.description: The declared architecture and language. Recorded intent, not an observation: Stage 1 does not inspect the media to confirm either. Both change what is installed and neither is inferable from a file name, which is why they are declared rather than guessed.

language.description: A BCP 47 language tag, for example en-US.
